items.text: A second overnight strike on the [[p:Crimean Bridge]] {{note: Road and rail bridge over the Kerch Strait that Russia opened in 2018, four years after annexing Crimea.}} brought down one arch and a stretch of roadway; Russia's Transport Ministry suspended traffic and reported no casualties. Kyiv Independent says a Ukrainian Flamingo missile was used. The same night Russian ballistic missiles hit two Kyiv bridges over the Dnipro, Mayor [[p:Vitali Klitschko]] says, disrupting water, heating and the metro; Ukrainian officials report two dead.
items.notes: Missile type per Kyiv Independent; not confirmed by Kyiv officially.

items.text: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says Ukraine held new online peace talks with US envoys [[p:Steve Witkoff]] and [[p:Jared Kushner]] and European officials, and that Ukrainian intelligence shows North Korea supplying Russia with new ballistic missiles. Axios reports the envoys will meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on 19 Nov on security guarantees; the Ramstein-format contact group meets at NATO on 17 Nov.

The bulk carrier Betul 8, carrying Romanian wheat to Egypt, capsized and sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone after its crew reported two sea-drone hits; all 12 crew were rescued. Security firm Diaplous counts 17 vessels attacked off Bulgaria and Romania since July. Officials in both countries point at Russia, but Sofia says there is no proof; Moscow has denied earlier attacks.

[[p:Donald Trump]] arrived in Manila for the ASEAN–US special summit and the first in-person [[p:Quad|Quadrilateral Security Dialogue]] leaders' meeting since 2024, with [[p:Narendra Modi]], [[p:Sanae Takaichi]] and [[p:Anthony Albanese]]. The White House itinerary then takes him to Shenzhen for [[p:APEC|Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation]], with a first Trump–[[p:Xi Jinping]]–[[p:Vladimir Putin]] meeting planned for 19 Nov; Trump says he might also meet [[p:Kim Jong Un]].

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands unveiled in Vienna a plan for a return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers, the first outside the EU, starting with a pilot of about 100 people in 2027 under the tightened EU return rules. UNHCR said it must respect human rights law; [[p:Human Rights Watch]] and NGOs criticised it and Spain rejected it.

The [[p:Sudanese Armed Forces]] are pushing into West Kordofan towards En Nahud, a gold hub that helps fund the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]]; the army says it took Al-Khuwai on 13 Nov and an RSF commander in North Darfur announced his defection. The Emergency Lawyers group blames an army airstrike in Abu Zabad for at least 13 deaths, which AP could not verify.
items.notes: Battlefield claims by the army; casualty claim by a rights group.
